dataset: NESO Historic Demand Data / Electrical Load Forecasting Benchmark task

source.license: NESO Open Data Licence; reuse and adaptation, including commercial reuse, with attribution 'Supported by National Energy SO Open Data.'

parse_and_data_quality.formats: 2022-2024 use day-first textual dates; 2025-2026 use ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Parse formats separately. A dayfirst=True mixed-format parse silently moves some ISO dates and creates spurious gaps; that incorrect initial pilot was discarded.
parse_and_data_quality.timestamp: Settlement date is Europe/London local midnight; map SETTLEMENT_PERIOD (1-based, 30 minutes each) to UTC, preserving 46/50-period DST days.
parse_and_data_quality.target: ND only; do not use TSD or forecast/actual indicator as model inputs.
parse_and_data_quality.features: At each UTC midnight origin, previous 168 hourly ND values plus six local-calendar sine/cosine signals for each of the next 24 UTC target hours; 312 float32 inputs and 24 continuous outputs. Hourly 30-minute MW observations are averaged, not summed.

pilot.task: Day-ahead 24-hour national Great Britain demand forecast
pilot.split: Chronological by target origin year: train 2022-2024, validation 2025, test 2026 through October 1 origins (2026 file ends October 2). No random row split.
pilot.preprocessing: Input and target standardization fit using training windows only. Full training partition in one batch per epoch.
pilot.training: Repository TabularMLP; CUDA RTX 3050 Laptop 6 GiB; Adam 1e-3; MSE; 30 epochs; seed 151/152/153 by architecture; best validation MSE checkpoint; test evaluated once.
pilot.metric: Test RMSE normalized by training target standard deviation (NRMSE); test MAE likewise normalized; MAPE; peak allocated CUDA memory.

disposition: KEEP PROVISIONALLY. The official data are anonymously downloadable under a permissive open licence; the fixed-window multi-output task is directly compatible with the repository's plain feedforward MLP; all 2022-2026 payloads were fully downloaded, parsed, hashed, and checked for row gaps; and full-batch MLP pilots beat simple baselines while remaining far from zero error. One chronological split, one seed per architecture, three vanilla architectures, partial-year 2026 test coverage, and no ADP/provider/runner integration limit the claim. No comparative ADP benefit is established.
